title: Upper motor neuron (MS) spinal lesion: spastic bladder -> bladder hypertonia on urodynamics
vignette: A 45-year-old man comes to the emergency department due to urinary incontinence. He was diagnosed with multiple sclerosis a year ago after he developed transient acute vision loss in his right eye. A few weeks ago, he began having difficulty with his balance and had several episodes of urinary incontinence. The patient's walking has improved since, but he continues to urinate involuntarily. He has noticed increasing urinary frequency and cannot control the urge to urinate. His vital signs are normal. On examination, the patient has mild spastic paraparesis with increased reflexes in the lower extremities; bilateral Babinski sign; and a thoracic sensory level to pain, temperature, and vibration. An MRI of the spine reveals a new demyelinating lesion in the mid-thoracic spinal cord. Which of the following abnormalities will most likely be found on this patient's urodynamic studies?

clues.text: diagnosed with multiple sclerosis a year ago
clues.note: Multiple sclerosis causes CNS demyelinating lesions; a spinal cord lesion produces an UPPER motor neuron pattern of bladder dysfunction.

clues.text: spastic paraparesis with increased reflexes in the lower extremities
clues.note: Spasticity and hyperreflexia are UPPER MOTOR NEURON signs, indicating loss of descending inhibitory control below the lesion.
Bilateral Babinski (upgoing toes) confirms an upper motor neuron lesion of the spinal cord.

clues.text: new demyelinating lesion in the mid-thoracic spinal cord
clues.note: A cord lesion ABOVE the sacral micturition center removes inhibitory control, producing a SPASTIC (overactive) bladder.

whatMatters: An UPPER MOTOR NEURON spinal cord lesion (MS) removes descending inhibition of the sacral micturition reflex, producing a SPASTIC/overactive (uninhibited) bladder: urgency, frequency, and incontinence. Urodynamics show BLADDER HYPERTONIA (detrusor overactivity) with little residual urine. Answer A.
strategy: Localize to UMN (spasticity, hyperreflexia, Babinski, cord lesion) -> spastic/overactive bladder. Urodynamics: detrusor overactivity = bladder HYPERTONIA, premature emptying, little residual urine. Reject findings of a LMN/flaccid bladder or obstruction: delayed emptying and large residual volume (flaccid/underactive bladder - LMN, cauda equina), and reduced urine flow/elevated urethral pressure (mechanical outlet obstruction, e.g., BPH/stricture).

eliminations.label: Delayed bladder emptying - underactive/flaccid bladder
eliminations.detail: WHAT IT IS: sluggish emptying from diminished detrusor tone. ❌ WHY IT FAILS: an UMN lesion causes OVERACTivity (premature emptying), not delayed emptying; delayed emptying suggests an underactive (LMN) bladder. ✅ Correct if: lower motor neuron/flaccid bladder.

eliminations.label: Elevated urethral pressure - mechanical obstruction
eliminations.detail: WHAT IT IS: increased outlet resistance (e.g., BPH, stricture). ❌ WHY IT FAILS: this indicates mechanical obstruction, not the detrusor overactivity of an UMN lesion. ✅ Correct if: bladder outlet obstruction.

eliminations.label: Large residual volume - flaccid (LMN) bladder
eliminations.detail: WHAT IT IS: a big post-void residual from poor emptying. ❌ WHY IT FAILS: that occurs with a FLACCID/underactive bladder (LMN lesion, cauda equina); the spastic UMN bladder empties with little residual. ✅ Correct if: flaccid bladder with overflow incontinence.

eliminations.label: Reduced urine flow - obstruction
eliminations.detail: WHAT IT IS: low flow rate suggesting outlet obstruction. ❌ WHY IT FAILS: it reflects mechanical obstruction along the urinary tract, not detrusor overactivity. ✅ Correct if: obstructive uropathy (e.g., prostate).

reasoning: MS caused a mid-thoracic cord lesion (UMN pattern: spasticity, hyperreflexia, Babinski)
A lesion above the sacral micturition center removes descending inhibition
This produces a spastic/overactive (uninhibited) bladder with urgency, frequency, incontinence
-> urodynamics show bladder hypertonia (detrusor overactivity); answer A
mechanism: Normal micturition is coordinated by a SACRAL reflex (S2-S4) that is modulated by DESCENDING pathways from the pontine micturition center and cortex (which provide voluntary/inhibitory control). An UPPER MOTOR NEURON lesion of the spinal cord ABOVE the sacral center - as in this MS patient with a mid-thoracic demyelinating lesion, spasticity, hyperreflexia, and Babinski signs - removes this descending inhibition, leaving the sacral reflex UNCHECKED. The result is a SPASTIC (uninhibited/OVERACTIVE) bladder: DETRUSOR OVERACTIVITY causes involuntary contractions at low volumes, producing urgency, frequency, and urge incontinence, with premature emptying and typically LOW post-void residual. On urodynamics this appears as BLADDER HYPERTONIA (increased detrusor pressure/reduced compliance). This contrasts with a LOWER MOTOR NEURON/sacral lesion (e.g., cauda equina), which gives a FLACCID, underactive bladder with a large residual volume and overflow incontinence, and with mechanical OUTLET OBSTRUCTION (elevated urethral pressure/reduced flow).

difficulty.label: 🧠 Knowledge
difficulty.text: First Aid Neuro/Renal > neurogenic bladder: UMN (suprasacral) lesion -> spastic/overactive bladder (detrusor overactivity, urgency/frequency, low residual); LMN (sacral/cauda equina) -> flaccid bladder (large residual, overflow); MS commonly causes spastic bladder.

difficulty.label: 📖 Comprehension
difficulty.text: UMN cord lesion -> loss of inhibition -> spastic/overactive bladder -> bladder hypertonia.

difficulty.label: 🔤 Vocab
difficulty.text: Unsure on UMN vs LMN bladder, detrusor overactivity, spastic vs flaccid bladder, micturition reflex, or post-void residual? Tell me which.

difficulty.label: 🨤 Distractor
difficulty.text: Delayed emptying/large residual = flaccid (LMN) bladder; elevated urethral pressure/reduced flow = mechanical obstruction.

difficulty.label: 🗒️ Other
difficulty.text: Bank: UMN (suprasacral) lesion -> spastic overactive bladder (hypertonia, urgency); LMN -> flaccid bladder (large residual).

keywords.back: Spastic/overactive -> bladder hypertonia (urgency, frequency, low residual)
Sacral reflex (S2-S4) modulated by pontine/cortical descending input

firstAid.detail: Renal > flaccid (LMN, large residual) vs obstruction (low flow).

memoryHook: Cut the brain's brakes on the bladder (UMN cord lesion) and it fires on its own - a spastic, hypertonic bladder that empties early and often.
